title.justification: The title is directly taken from the provided paper citation.
title.quote: On Extractive and Abstractive Neural Document Summarization with Transformer Language Models

analysis.description: The paper proposes a method for neural document summarization that combines extractive and abstractive approaches using transformer language models. The method first extracts important sentences from long documents and then uses a transformer-based model conditioned on these sentences to generate abstractive summaries. The paper demonstrates that this approach outperforms traditional seq2seq methods and state-of-the-art models by producing more abstractive summaries with higher ROUGE scores, notably without using a copy mechanism.

type.justification: The paper explores and evaluates a method for document summarization, performing experiments to compare the proposed method against existing models using datasets like arXiv and PubMed.
type.quote: We provide an application to text summarization of the arXiv and PubMed datasets, and show that our model outperforms other popular summarization techniques.

name.justification: The paper specifically addresses methods for document summarization, combining extractive and abstractive techniques.
name.quote: We present a method to produce abstractive summaries of long documents that exceed several thousand words via neural abstractive summarization.

name.justification: The paper's major contribution is using a Transformer Language Model for generating document summaries conditioned on extracted sentences.
name.quote: We use a transformer (Vaswani et al. 2017) language model (TLM) architecture identical to (Radford et al. 2019).

is_contributed.justification: The paper proposes the use of a Transformer Language Model for summarization conditioned on extracted content, which is a primary contribution.
is_contributed.quote: We demonstrate that transformer language models are surprisingly effective at summarizing long scientific articles and outperform typical seq2seq approaches, even without a copy mechanism.

is_executed.justification: The paper mentions executing the Transformer Language Model using GPUs for training.
is_executed.quote: We trained the language model for 5 days on 16 V100 GPUs on a single Nvidia DGX-2 box.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares the performance of the Transformer Language Model with other summarization models using ROUGE scores.
is_compared.quote: We compare our results to several previously proposed extractive and abstractive models.
